title: Logical Sequences
source: MindSpark Grade 7 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 1: Logical Sequences
learningGoals: Identify and extend complex number series involving squares, Fibonacci sums, and two-level differences.
Decode letter-number mixed sequences by tracking each component independently.
Apply multiple rules simultaneously to solve decreasing and alternating sequences.
coreIdeas: When the differences are not constant, write the second-level differences — they often form an AP.
Fibonacci-style series: each term = sum of the two terms before it. Check by adding backwards.
For letter-number mixed sequences, split into two tracks and find each rule independently.

workedExamples.solution: Terms are perfect squares: 1²=1, 2²=4, 3²=9, 4²=16, 5²=25. Next term = 6² = 36.
workedExamples.concept: Perfect square series — nth term = n²

workedExamples.solution: Check: 2+3=5, 3+5=8, 5+8=13, 8+13=21. Each term = sum of previous two (Fibonacci rule). Next = 13+21 = 34.
workedExamples.concept: Fibonacci-style series — each term is the sum of the two preceding terms

workedExamples.solution: Differences: 5-3=2, 9-5=4, 15-9=6, 23-15=8. The differences are 2, 4, 6, 8 — AP with gap +2. Next difference: 10. Answer: 23+10 = 33.
workedExamples.concept: Two-step difference series — differences themselves form an AP

mission.missionPromise: By the end you will decode Fibonacci patterns, two-step differences, and mixed letter-number sequences — skills that ace Olympiad paper Section A!
mission.successCelebration: Award an XP pulse and a 'Sequence Sleuth' badge after every group. Final trophy: 'Sequence Vault Unlocked'.

microLessonPattern: Coach opens with a competitive hook — 'Top scorers solve this in under 10 seconds!'
Coach writes one worked series on the board, labelling each step clearly.
Coach reads the practice question aloud and invites the student to spot the rule.
Student states the rule first, then gives the answer.
Instant feedback praises correct rule identification, not just the final number.
Review prompt asks student to name the pattern type before moving on.

beats.teacherLine: Welcome to Grade 7 Logical Sequences — where patterns get serious! You already know AP and GP. Now we level up: perfect square series, Fibonacci-style sums, and two-step difference patterns. These appear in every competitive exam. Learn these three upgrades and you will solve sequence questions faster than most adults!
beats.boardAction: Write 'Grade 7 Sequences — 3 Upgrades' at top. List: (1) Square series: 1, 4, 9, 16... (2) Fibonacci: each term = sum of previous two. (3) Two-step diff: differences form their own AP.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Quick check: 1, 4, 9, 16, __ — what is the pattern and the next term?

svgAnimation.text: 3. Two-step diff: gaps form their own AP

beats.teacherLine: Watch me crack a two-step difference series live. Series: 3, 5, 9, 15, 23, __ Step 1: write differences underneath — 2, 4, 6, 8. Step 2: those differences go up by 2 each time. Next difference must be 10. Step 3: answer is 23+10 = 33. Two levels deep — that is the pro move!
beats.boardAction: Write: 3  5  9  15  23  __. Below: diffs 2  4  6  8. Below that: +2 +2 +2. Circle next diff = 10. Show 23+10=33.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Your turn: 2, 4, 8, 14, 22, __ — write the differences first, then find the next term.
beats.expectedStudentResponse: Differences are 2, 4, 6, 8 — next diff is 10, answer is 32.

beats.teacherLine: You are now armed with three advanced sequence tools. Before each question, name the pattern type — square, Fibonacci, two-step diff, or a combo. Naming the pattern earns you half the XP even if the final number is off. Work through Groups A to H and aim for the Sequence Vault trophy!
beats.boardAction: Show a decision flowchart: Is each term n²? → Square series. Does term = previous two added? → Fibonacci. Are differences forming an AP? → Two-step diff. Is it letters + numbers? → Split tracks.
beats.checkpointPrompt: State one key difference between a Fibonacci series and a two-step difference series.
beats.expectedStudentResponse: Fibonacci adds the two previous terms; two-step diff adds an increasing gap to the last term.
beats.fallbackHint: Fibonacci: term = (term-1) + (term-2). Two-step: the gaps between terms themselves form an AP — you add a growing difference each time.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! The squares are hiding in plain sight — 1, 4, 9, 16... recognise them instantly and you gain 5 seconds on every exam!

boardDemo.title: Perfect Square Series
boardDemo.teacherLine: Memorise squares up to 15² = 225. When you see 4, 9, 16, 25 — your brain should shout 'square series' immediately. That instant recognition is the competitive edge.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Look at: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36 — can you name each as a perfect square?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: 9, 16, 25, 36, __ — name the series type and the next term!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Spot on! 3², 4², 5², 6², so next is 7² = 49. Your square recognition is sharp!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: 9=3², 16=4², 25=5², 36=6². Count up: next square root is 7. So 7²=49.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: 25, 36, 49, 64, __ — what is the next perfect square?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Fibonacci is famous in maths, art, and nature. Each term is the sum of the two before it — a sneaky but beautiful rule!

boardDemo.title: Fibonacci Rule — Sum of Previous Two
steps: Rule: each term = previous term + term before it
boardDemo.teacherLine: To verify Fibonacci, always add the two terms BEFORE the one you are checking. If the sum matches, you have a Fibonacci series. Then add the last two terms for the answer.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Series: 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, __ — add 13 and 21 in your head. What do you get?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, __ — check if it is Fibonacci, then find the next term!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Yes! 3+4=7 ✓, 4+7=11 ✓, 7+11=18 ✓. It is Fibonacci! 11+18=29. You spotted the Fibonacci fingerprint!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: check 4+7 — do you get 11? Check 7+11 — do you get 18? Yes! So add the last two: 11+18=29.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, __ — is this Fibonacci? Give the next term.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! The differences between terms are hiding their OWN pattern. Two layers deep — this is serious detective work!

boardDemo.title: Two-Step Differences — AP Within Gaps
boardDemo.teacherLine: Always write the differences under the series. If those differences are not equal, write the SECOND level of differences. One of the levels will always be constant in a well-formed series.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Series: 1, 3, 7, 13, 21, __ — write the differences: 2, 4, 6, 8. What is the next difference?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: 4, 6, 10, 16, 24, __ — write both levels of differences and find the next term!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Excellent! Diffs: 2, 4, 6, 8 — gap +2, so next diff = 10. 24+10 = 34. Two-level detective work, done!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: 6-4=2, 10-6=4, 16-10=6, 24-16=8. Diffs are 2,4,6,8. The next diff is 10. Add 10 to 24.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Practice: 0, 2, 6, 12, 20, __ — show the two difference levels and give the answer.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! What if the step itself gets bigger every time — +1, +2, +3, +4? The staircase grows as you climb it!

boardDemo.title: Increasing Steps — Gap Grows by 1 Each Time
boardDemo.teacherLine: If the differences are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5... the steps are simply counting upwards. Find which step you are on, add 1 to it, and add that to the last term.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Series: 3, 4, 6, 9, 13, __ — differences are 1, 2, 3, 4. What is the next difference?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: 5, 6, 8, 11, 15, __ — identify the increasing step and find the next term!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Perfect! Diffs: 1, 2, 3, 4 — next step is 5. 15+5=20. Increasing-step sequence mastered!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: 6-5=1, 8-6=2, 11-8=3, 15-11=4. Steps are 1,2,3,4. Next step is 5. Add 5 to 15.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: 0, 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, __ — state the step pattern and the next term.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Numbers shrinking by division or subtraction with a twist — the multiplier makes it tricky. Stay sharp!

boardDemo.title: Decreasing Series — Divide or Subtract with Pattern
steps: Rule: divide by 2 each step (GP with ratio 1/2)
boardDemo.teacherLine: Decreasing series often use a constant divisor — that is a GP going down. Divide any term by the one before it. If the ratio is the same (like 1/2 or 1/3), multiply the last term by that ratio.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Series: 243, 81, 27, 9, __ — what do you divide to get from one term to the next?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: 162, 54, 18, 6, __ — find the ratio and the next term!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Brilliant! 54/162=1/3, 18/54=1/3. Ratio = ÷3 each step. 6÷3=2. Decreasing GP cracked!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: divide 54 by 162 — you get 1/3. Same for 18÷54=1/3. Keep dividing by 3: 6÷3=2.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: 128, 64, 32, 16, __ — name the ratio and the next term.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Two patterns in one — letters doing one thing, numbers doing another. Split and conquer!

boardDemo.title: Mixed Sequences — Two Tracks
steps: Letter track: A=1, C=3, E=5, G=7 → +2 each → next: 9 = I
boardDemo.teacherLine: Letters and numbers can each follow completely different rules. One might be AP, the other GP. Always separate them, solve each, then put the answer back together.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Series: B4, D8, F16, H32, __ — what rule do the letters follow? What rule do the numbers follow?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: A1, C4, E9, G16, __ — the numbers are perfect squares! Find both tracks and combine.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Outstanding! Letters: A,C,E,G,I (+2 positions). Numbers: 1,4,9,16,25 (perfect squares). Answer: I25. Double-pattern champion!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: letters A,C,E,G — gap=+2, next is I. Numbers 1,4,9,16 — those are 1²,2²,3²,4², next is 5²=25. Combine: I25.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: Z2, X6, V18, T54, __ — letters decrease, numbers ×3. Give the next pair.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Some series hide TWO interleaved rules — odd positions follow one rule, even positions follow another. Separate the odd and even terms!

boardDemo.title: Alternating Series — Odd and Even Terms Separate
boardDemo.teacherLine: When a series looks irregular, separate the odd-indexed terms from the even-indexed terms. Each sub-series almost always follows a simple AP or GP rule.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Series: 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 18, 10, __ — odd terms: 1, 4, 7, 10 (+3 AP). Even terms: 2, 6, 18 (×3 GP). What is the 8th term?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: 5, 1, 10, 3, 15, 9, 20, __ — separate odd and even positions, then find the next term!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Superb! Odd: 5, 10, 15, 20 (+5). Even: 1, 3, 9, 27 (×3). The 8th term is an even-position term: 9×3=27. Alternating series decoded!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: write only the even-position terms: 1, 3, 9. That is ×3 each time (GP). The 8th term is the 4th even-position term: 9×3=27.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: 2, 1, 4, 3, 8, 9, 16, __ — separate the tracks. Which is the next even-position term?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code — FAST! This is the competitive round. Name the pattern type in 5 seconds, answer in 10. Olympiad champions do exactly this!

boardDemo.title: Speed Round — All 7 Sequence Types
steps: Speed tip: name the type first — it halves your solving time
boardDemo.teacherLine: In Olympiad exams, you get about 30 seconds per sequence question. Name the type aloud, write the differences if needed, and commit to the answer. Speed + accuracy = top score.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: I will fire 4 sequences. Name the type AND the answer for each. Ready?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: INCREDIBLE! Q1: diffs 4,6,8,10,12 → 30+12=42. Q2: Fibonacci (3+4=7, 4+7=11, 7+11=18). Q3: ÷2 GP → 4. Q4: letters +2, numbers ×2 → I32. Sequence Vault fully unlocked!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Q1 diffs are 4,6,8,10 — next is 12, so 30+12=42. Q2: 4+7=11, 7+11=18. Q3: 8÷2=4. Q4: letters A,C,E,G,I and numbers 2,4,8,16,32 → I32.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Final: name the 4 most common sequence types at Grade 7 level, give one example of each.
